title: Orchids from a test tube
body: A nursery wants to sell thousands of identical orchid plants of one rare, high-quality variety. Growing them from seed is slow, and the seedlings differ from the parent. The nursery instead uses tissue culture. A worker removes a few cells from the growing tip of a healthy parent orchid and places them in a sterile container with an artificial nutrient medium. Within a few weeks the cells divide rapidly and form a small mass of undifferentiated cells. This mass is then shifted to a second medium. Soon, tiny plantlets with shoots and roots appear. These plantlets are later placed in pots of soil, where they grow into mature plants. In a few months the nursery has thousands of orchids, all free from disease and all showing the same flower colour and shape as the parent plant.
